title: Political Connections and the Cost of Bank Loans

scopes.description: Complete author-documented workflow. The supplied variant is an internet appendix with supplementary loan-spread analyses and table notes, but contains no runnable source, full workflow, or analysis data.

requirements.description: The appendix analyses single bank-loan spreads and identifies borrower political-connection/board information, firm and loan controls, and instrument inputs based on firm age and headquarters distance. Its supplemental samples include a 2003–2008 financial-crisis test and 2005–2007 election tests, with additional matching and covenant-restricted analyses. The appendix defers many variable definitions to Table 1 of the paper and does not provide analysis data, raw input files, stored-field names, identifiers/joins, complete sample construction, or a compatible acquisition route for the full workflow.

issues.description: The supplied inventory contains only the internet appendix PDF. It has reported supplementary tables and references definitions in the paper, but no executable programs, README/data guide, entry points, complete analysis data, or producer-consumer instructions. The full workflow and analysis-input route therefore remain unresolved.

evidence.description: The appendix reports a loan-spread model with political-connection, firm, and loan controls, and says other variable definitions are in Table 1 of the paper.
evidence.quote: The dependent variable is the log loan spread.

evidence.description: The financial-crisis appendix sample covers 2003–2008, uses the IMF Banking Crisis Database definition, and restricts firms by stable political-connection status.
evidence.quote: This sample includes only firms without change of their political connection status during the crisis period 2007-2008.

evidence.description: The first-stage appendix specifies log firm age and headquarters distances to the state capital and Washington, DC as instruments.

evidence.description: The appendix describes propensity-score matching of politically connected and unconnected loan observations, including bootstrapped inference.
evidence.quote: The propensity scores are estimated by a probit model.

evidence.description: The mid-term election analysis uses 2005–2007 loan deals, party-specific board indicators, and before/after borrowing restrictions.
The covenant analysis retains loans without capital-expenditure restrictions and liquidity covenants.
evidence.quote: Only loans without capital expenditure restriction and liquidity covenants are included in the sample.

actions.description: Obtain the executable research package and complete loan-level input specification before assessing full-pipeline execution.
steps: Request or locate the complete author-provided code package, README/data guide, entry points, supporting programs, and any author-prepared loan-level analysis files.

Request the paper Table 1 definitions and identify the actual input files/products, stored fields, loan and firm identifiers/crosswalks, full periods, sample restrictions, construction, and author-documented acquisition/preparation route for each analysis branch.
After the workflow is supplied, trace the producer-consumer order and assess the supplied inputs and prescribed software; do not independently reconstruct the historical loan-level research data.
validation: Confirm each documented main and appendix analysis stage has a supplied entry point and documented inputs, with any missing producer or handoff retained as an unresolved issue.
Verify candidate loan/firm fields, identifiers, variable construction, and branch-specific coverage against the author specification before recording an input route as compatible.

review_notes: This is a document-only release. The appendix reports supplementary results and describes some branch-specific samples and variables, but does not provide analysis data or code; no analysis-only execution scope is supported.
